[00:00:00] Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I run... uh, I'm the AE for your account at Redwood. With me is Liam our systems engineer and Sofia from customer success. Quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Alex (CTO): Alex here, Priya and Tom from Cobalt.
[00:00:16] Priya (Security): Hi all.
[00:00:20] Maya: Great. We're going to walk through our data retention and PII controls, show both the Console UI and the API toggles. We want to make sure you can meet your compliance needs for payments data. Liam, you want to kick off?
[00:00:33] Liam (SE): Yep. I'll share my screen. So first slide is high level: we support per-route request storage toggles, field-level PII redaction, and selectable logging levels. On the Console you can do this without code but everything is also available via our REST API.
[00:00:50] Tom (Eng): Quick question — by "request storage toggle" you mean you can turn off storing requests for specific routes?
[00:00:56] Liam: Exactly. You can set "store_requests: false" at the route or model config. When off, the system will not persist request/response bodies to long-term storage, but we still maintain ephemeral traces for debugging for a configurable short window.
[00:01:12] Priya: What about PII? We need to redact card numbers, CVVs, names, emails — is that automated?
[00:01:18] Liam: We have built-in PII detectors plus the ability to add custom regex and named-entity patterns. By default we run a redaction pipeline before persistence; you can choose mask (****), type-hint, or remove. The Console shows an example.
[00:01:33] [screen share noise]
[00:01:35] Liam: Here on the Console under Project -> Data Controls, you see toggles per route. I'll flip on one called "payments-proxy/no-store" and set retention to zero days. You can see the UI warns you that full request bodies won't be available for future debugging.
[00:01:54] Alex: If we set retention to zero, are we still able to get traces for incidents?
[00:01:59] Liam: There is a short ephemeral buffer — typically 1 hour by default — which can be configured in Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted we keep short-term traces for debugging and then delete or redact according to the rule.
[00:02:12] Priya: How deterministic is the PII detector? I've seen false positives and negatives with other systems.
[00:02:18] Liam: Good question; detection uses ensembles: regex for strict patterns (like PANs), ML NER models for names/addresses, and a rules engine. For PANs we use Luhn check to confirm. For edge cases we recommend shipping a small sample of sanitized logs so we can tune the regex/model thresholds.
[00:02:38] Tom: Is that tuning automatic or manual?
[00:02:41] Liam: We provide both: auto-suggested patterns from your sample plus manual overrides. And in Dedicated/Private you can host custom models or on-prem inference for detection.
[00:02:52] Priya: Encryption in transit is standard, but what about stored data? Where are keys managed?
[00:02:58] Maya: We encrypt at rest by default. You can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted there's Redwood-managed KMS but we offer customer OMS keys on enterprise plans.
[00:03:12] Priya: Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for all access.
[00:03:16] Sofia (CSM): We capture access events and admin actions. In Private deployments those logs can be routed to your SIEM over syslog or to an S3 bucket in your account. In Hosted we provide 90d audit retention by default with exports available.
[00:03:31] Alex: Competitor question — how does this compare to what others do?
[00:03:35] Maya: Most providers let you disable storing requests, but the differentiator for us is fine-grained per-route policy plus the PII redaction pipeline and the option to host the entire control plane privately. Also we have per-token cost visibility and auto-batching features that help keep unit costs down even when doing redaction.
[00:03:53] [00:04:00] Liam: Back to Console: I'll open an example route config JSON. You can see fields: "store_requests": false, "redaction": {"mode": "mask", "rules": ["pan","email","ssn"]} — note these are examples in the UI. 
[00:04:18] Tom: I noticed "redaction" block — can we get returns (i.e., logs) with placeholders like <PAN_REDACTED> instead of stars?
[00:04:24] Liam: Yes, we support type-hint placeholders. You can also include metadata tags like redaction version and rule id for traceability.
[00:04:33] Priya: Do you store the original unredacted text anywhere in the chain?
[00:04:37] Liam: Not in the normal flow. For Hosted, originals are not persisted if you enable the no-store toggle. In cases where customers request escrowed originals for legal reasons we can negotiate a workflow but that's only for Dedicated/Private and requires strict access controls.
[00:04:52] Alex: For our compliance we may need to retain some attributes for fraud detection, but not full payloads. Can you do partial retention?
[00:04:58] Liam: Yes — per-route you can configure field-level selectors to persist only specific metadata (e.g., hashed PAN prefix, transaction id, latency) and redact everything else. We also support hashing with salt on stored fields.
[00:05:12] [00:05:20] Tom: How about the API side — can we toggle this programmatically during a rollout?
[00:05:24] Liam: Absolutely. The Admin API lets you PATCH route config. We also have feature flags in the Console and SDKs. Everything is auditable.
[00:05:34] Priya: Will toggling store_requests off affect model performance or latency?
[00:05:39] Liam: Minimal impact. The heavy lifting is inference; persistence is async. When you disable storage it can slightly improve throughput because we skip serialization/persistence steps. But caching layers and batching are the dominant factors for latency.
[00:05:51] Alex: Cost impact — if we keep redaction on vs off, any cost delta?
[00:05:55] Maya: Redaction adds small CPU overhead and potentially extra egress if you send tokens to a detection service, but for most workloads it's a low-single-digit percentage of token cost. We'll include estimated numbers in the follow-up benchmarking sheet.
[00:06:10] [00:06:30] Liam: Now I'll demo a live example. I'm going to run a sample payment request through the API with store_requests: true and show the audit log. Then flip the route to no-store and run again.
[00:06:45] [typing/click sounds]
[00:06:49] Liam: First run — you can see raw request is persisted in the console trace (we blurred some parts on the demo). The redaction pipeline flagged a 16-digit number and masked it.
[00:07:03] Priya: That Luhn check is useful.
[00:07:06] Liam: Now flipping to no-store... run second request... and the trace shows a minimal ephemeral trace: request id, model id, latency, and redaction summary. No body.
[00:07:20] Tom: Good. For incident investigations how would we get the full body if needed?
[00:07:24] Liam: If necessary, we can configure a secure escalation path: ephemeral retrieval with strict RBAC and audit logging, or escrowed storage in your Private environment. That's part of the Dedicated/Private engagement.
[00:07:36] Priya: We need SSO and RBAC for access to unredacted data.
[00:07:40] Sofia: We support SAML/SSO and role-based permissions. For Private, you can hook into your IdP and define fine-grained roles for retrieval workflows.
[00:07:49] [00:08:00] Alex: Anything about downstream logs? We push logs into our ELK. If Redwood has redacted data, can we still correlate events?
[00:08:06] Liam: Yes, we inject stable identifiers and hashed fields for correlation. You can route logs to your ELK; those logs will reflect redacted values but include correlation keys and rule-ids for debugging.
[00:08:19] Priya: Can we define retention windows per environment? Like shorter in prod than staging?
[00:08:24] Liam: Yep. Policies are scoped to project/environment/route. We typically recommend shorter retention in prod for PII-sensitive data and longer in staging for dev diagnostics.
[00:08:34] [00:08:50] Tom: For POC, what's the recommended mode? Hosted with no-store toggles or Dedicated trial?
[00:08:55] Maya: Start with Hosted and use no-store + redaction rules. If you need guaranteed isolation, Dedicated is the next step and Private for full on-prem. We'll propose a POC plan in the follow-up with specific benchmarks.
[00:09:08] Priya: Can you share the redaction whitepaper or docs on false positive rates?
[00:09:12] Maya: Yes — action item for us to send that pack.
[00:09:18] [mid-call chatter, clarifications]
[00:20:00] Liam: Jumping ahead to Audit & Compliance slide — we keep a detailed audit trail: who changed policies, when, and the prior value. For any retrieval of unredacted content there's an approval workflow logged.
[00:20:15] Priya: What about encryption keys rotation?
[00:20:18] Maya: Rotation is supported and can be scheduled. In BYOK you control key rotation cadence.
[00:20:25] Alex: For POC metrics, we care about latency (p95), cost per 1k tokens, and detection accuracy.
[00:20:31] Liam: We'll run KV-cache benchmarks plus a redaction pass, and provide p50/p95 numbers and cost deltas.
[00:20:38] Tom: Any limits on custom regex rules? Performance wise?
[00:20:42] Liam: Very complex regex can add CPU, but we sandbox the rules. We recommend simple anchored patterns for heavy filters and ML detectors for fuzzy matches.
[00:20:52] [00:30:00] Maya: Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[00:30:05] Maya: 1) We'll send SOC2/security packet and redaction docs. 2) Liam will run the benchmark with your sample dataset. 3) We'll schedule a POC scoping call to discuss Dedicated baseline. 4) Cobalt to share sample logs and list of fields to retain.
[00:30:22] Alex: Sounds good. Priya, any outstanding blockers from security?
[00:30:26] Priya: Not for now, we just need to review the SOC2 and see the false-positive stats. Also want to understand escrowed workflows if legal requires it.
[00:30:36] Maya: We'll include escrow options in the POC doc.
[00:30:40] Tom: Timeline — can we have benchmarks in two weeks?
[00:30:43] Liam: Yes, we'll aim for that.
[00:30:47] [closing pleasantries]
[00:30:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and the sheet.
[00:31:00] Alex: Thanks, bye.
[00:31:03] Priya: Thanks.
[00:31:05] (call ended)
